cover.headline: India's car-glass leader, priced for a float-glass boom that rests on trade protection
cover.lead: Asahi India Glass (AIS) makes ~80% of the glass in Indian passenger cars and owns three float-glass lines. After a ₹2,835 cr build-out (FY24-26) and a ₹1,000 cr QIP, earnings turned: Q1FY27 EBITDA was ₹325 cr (23.0% margin) and profit ₹149 cr, 2.7 times a year earlier, with float glass doing most of the lifting. We forecast EBITDA of ₹1,326 / ₹1,428 / ₹1,531 cr for FY27-29E. The only broker we could find, ICICI Securities, values AIS on **EV/EBITDA (22x FY28E, target ₹1,050)**. The house rule (AIS's own forward EV/EBITDA median since 2021, 18.1x, cut by the 13.4% auto-component de-rating) gives **15.5x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,480 cr, less ₹2,202 cr of net debt = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹869, DCF ₹297. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Automotive glass: a near-monopoly, but Maruti sets the price
arguments.p: AIS supplies ~80% of passenger-vehicle glass in India and sits inside Maruti's Kharkhoda plant. Gross auto revenue grew from ₹1,346 cr (FY21) to ₹3,383 cr (FY26) and +22% in Q1FY27 on record car output and more glass per car (sunroofs, laminated side glass, HUD-ready windshields). But the EBITDA margin has stayed at 12-18% for six years: Maruti (a promoter with 10.6%) bought ₹873 cr in FY26 and ₹301 cr in Q1FY27 alone. We model auto +{{as.segments.0.growth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.2|pct0}} at a {{as.segments.0.marginPct.0|pct}} margin.

arguments.h: Float glass: the profit engine, and the risk
arguments.p: Float glass earned a 34% EBITDA margin at the FY22 import-price peak and 18% in FY25. The third line (Soniyana) now feeds the auto business, and in Q1FY27 float segment EBIT tripled to ₹117 cr (21.5% of gross revenue; ~28.0% EBITDA by our estimate). In Aug-2026 the government added a minimum import price on clear float glass, but for one year only. We assume {{as.segments.1.marginPct.0|pct}} / {{as.segments.1.marginPct.1|pct}} / {{as.segments.1.marginPct.2|pct}}: high, fading as protection lapses and new capacity arrives.

arguments.h: Capital-hungry, with low returns so far
arguments.p: ROCE fell from 21% (FY22-23) to 11% (FY26) through the build-out, ROE to 10.5% after the QIP, and another ₹2,000 cr of greenfield float, coatings and processing capex was approved in Jan-2026. With capex of ₹850-1,000 cr a year in our model, free cash flow stays near zero and net debt near ₹2,000-2,250 cr (1.5x EBITDA). Growth is being bought with capital at returns below its cost; the chairman himself says the next phase must be about returns.

arguments.h: Valuation: the market pays for the good quarter
arguments.p: At ₹959 AIS trades at 17.8x our Sep-28E EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) and 37.3x FY28E EPS, close to its own 18.1x forward EV/EBITDA median since 2021, while auto-component stocks sat 13.4% below their five-year EV/EBITDA medians on 30-Sep-2026. ICICI's 22x applied to our FY28E EBITDA would give ~₹1,148: the gap is the multiple, not the estimates. We see no reason to pay a premium for earnings that lean on trade protection.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether float margins hold with the minimum import price in force from 18-Aug-2026, and auto growth against a softer base.

Trade policy: the one-year minimum import price on clear float glass (expires Aug-2027 unless extended); the government's decision on continuing anti-dumping duties on Malaysian float glass after the 2026 sunset review.
Capex: timetable, location and capacity of the ₹2,000 cr greenfield float/coatings/processing programme; Patan phase 3 and 4.
Festive-season car sales (Oct-Dec 2026) and Maruti's volumes, the single biggest driver of auto glass.
Energy and soda-ash prices: a float line burns natural gas around the clock; other auto suppliers reported gas and fuel costs rising with the West Asia conflict in Q1FY27.

sections.title: Two glass businesses under one roof: car glass for every Indian car maker, and float glass for buildings and for itself

blocks.p: Asahi India Glass (AIS) began in 1987 as a joint venture of the Labroo family, Asahi Glass of Japan (now AGC Inc., still the largest shareholder at 21.2%) and Maruti Udyog (now Maruti Suzuki, 10.6%). **Automotive glass** (gross segment revenue ₹3,383 cr in FY26) makes laminated windshields, tempered side and back glass, sunroofs and encapsulated glass for cars, trucks, buses, tractors, railways and metros, and glass for refrigerators and washing machines; it holds ~80% of Indian passenger-vehicle glass. **Float glass** (₹1,754 cr, of which ₹492 cr sold to the auto business) runs three float lines (Roorkee, Taloja and, since FY25, Soniyana in Rajasthan; 2,150 tonnes a day) and coats and processes glass for buildings (~12% of architectural glass, ~26% of value-added architectural glass). A **consumer** arm (AIS Windows, Glasxperts, Windshield Experts) sells windows and replacement car glass directly. In all: 15 manufacturing facilities and 11 sub-assembly units-cum-warehouses; auto glass at Bawal, Chennai, Patan, Roorkee and Pune, plus an on-site unit inside Maruti's Kharkhoda campus.

sections.title: Forty years from a single-customer windshield plant to an integrated glass maker, funded three times by shareholders

blocks.p: AIS started as a single-plant, single-product, single-customer business: windshields for Maruti. It added tempered glass and new car makers, entered float glass by merging Floatglass India (Taloja) in 2003, also runs a float line at Roorkee (cold-repaired in FY25-26) and added a third at Soniyana, Rajasthan. Shareholders have funded it three times: ₹1.87 cr at start-up (1987), a ₹250 cr rights issue (2013) and a ₹1,000 cr QIP in Sep-2025 (1.18 crore shares at ₹844.8). The share count rose from 24.31 cr to 25.49 cr, so FY26 EPS fell 9% while profit fell 6%.

sections.title: Cars: record volumes (+17% PV output in Q1FY27). Float glass: a commodity that lives on trade protection

blocks.p: India sold a record 4.64 mn passenger vehicles in FY26 (+7.9%) and exported 0.91 mn (+17.5%); PV production was ~5.5 mn (+9%) and 1.45 mn in Q1FY27 (+17%), helped by the Sep-2025 GST cut. Each car also carries more glass: SUVs, panoramic roofs, laminated side glass, acoustic and solar-control glass, and windshields ready for head-up displays and ADAS cameras. Float glass is different: India's clear-glass prices are set by imports, mostly from Malaysia (85% of imports, 361,000 t), China and Thailand. Anti-dumping duties on Malaysian glass were recommended for five more years after a 2026 review, and on 18-Aug-2026 the government added a minimum import price of ₹34,000 per tonne on clear float glass of 4-12 mm, for one year. The chairman calls this "temporary support" against "distorted competition" (AR FY26).

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the car-glass market grows with car output plus 4-5% a year of content, and AIS already has ~80% of it: its auto growth will track the industry, no more. The float market is cyclical and import-driven; today's margins are flattered by Soniyana running full and by trade protection that has an end date.

bullets: **Cars: the tailwind reaches AIS, with a few points of content on top.** Auto revenue grew 3-5 points faster than car output in FY26 and Q1FY27, consistent with more glass per car. With ~80% share there is no share left to gain.
**But the margin does not follow.** Auto segment EBITDA margin was 16.1% in FY25 and 14.8% in FY26 despite record volumes; Q1FY27's ~17.4% (our estimate) came with cheaper in-house float glass.

**Float: the tailwind is policy and capacity, not demand.** Float growth in FY26-Q1FY27 came from the new Soniyana line; the minimum import price helps prices from Aug-2026 for a year. Neither is a durable advantage.

sections.kicker: Segment: automotive glass (~60% of gross revenue)
sections.title: Automotive glass: ~80% share and growing with car content; the margin is set by customers and costs

blocks.p: Gross automotive revenue was ₹3,383 cr in FY26 (+12.4%; external sales ₹3,369 cr, +12.7%) and ₹949 cr in Q1FY27 (+22.1%). AIS supplies every Indian car maker and supported glass for 13 model launches in FY26; laminated capacity is ~10 mn pieces and tempered ~7.5 mn car sets a year. Segment EBITDA (result + depreciation) was 14.8% in FY26, down from ~16% in FY24-25 as depreciation, staff and new-plant costs rose (ICICI Securities: auto EBIT +1% YoY in Q4FY26). Q1FY27 segment EBIT rose to ₹128 cr (13.4% of gross revenue vs 10.6%); with depreciation the EBITDA margin was ~17.4% by our estimate, helped by raw glass now coming from AIS's own Soniyana line rather than imports. Brownfield work continues at Patan (phase 3 under way, phase 4 initiated), Chennai and Bawal.

sections.title: Float glass: Soniyana doubled the profit in a year; protection and prices decide what happens next

blocks.p: AIS makes float glass on three lines (2150 tonnes a day in total): Roorkee, Taloja and Soniyana (Rajasthan), commissioned in FY25 and now used fully for the auto business's raw glass. Gross float revenue was ₹1,754 cr in FY26 (external ₹1,262 cr; ₹492 cr sold to the auto business), and ₹545 cr in Q1FY27 (+41.0%). Segment EBIT went from ₹37 cr (Q1FY26) to ₹117 cr (Q1FY27), 21.5% of gross revenue. The history is a warning: float EBITDA margins were 34.3% in FY22 and 31.4% in FY23 when import prices were high, then 20.2% (FY24) and 18.4% (FY25) when Malaysian and Chinese glass flowed in. ICICI Securities saw architectural EBIT +133% YoY in Q4FY26. AIS does not disclose float volumes, prices or utilisation.

sections.title: Consumer glass: windows and windshield repair, small and only now profitable

blocks.p: AIS Consumer Glass Solutions (AIS Windows, Glasxperts, Windshield Experts) was formed by merging four downstream subsidiaries from Jul-2025 (AIS owns 98.5%). It sells uPVC and aluminium windows, interior and façade glass through dealers and two experience centres, and repairs and replaces car glass through 151 service centres in 79 cities (cashless insurance claims). Reported "Others" gross revenue excluding other income was ₹754 cr in FY26 (incl. sales to other segments); our balancing line (Screener operating profit less auto and float EBITDA) earned ~₹37 cr (4.9%) in FY26 and lost money in FY21-24. The chairman: "We have remained small and slow in this business… I am extremely optimistic about exponential growth of AIS-CG." sections.title: Maruti Suzuki: the biggest customer, a 10.6% shareholder and a promoter

blocks.p: One customer bought ₹872.97 cr of automotive glass in FY26 (₹656.93 cr in FY25): Maruti Suzuki, which also owns 10.59% of AIS and is classified as a promoter. That is 17.5% of FY26 revenue and ~26% of external auto sales. In Q1FY27 sales to Maruti were ₹301.42 cr (21% of revenue), and shareholders approved related-party transactions with Maruti of up to ₹1,500 cr for FY27 (30% of FY26 turnover) at the 18-Sep-2026 AGM. AIS runs an on-site assembly unit inside Maruti's new Kharkhoda plant (glass goes straight to the line on returnable racks). AGC, the 21% shareholder, provides technical support; it has ~12% of the world float-glass market and ~30% of auto glass (Screener company profile).

bullets: **Good for volume:** Maruti is India's largest car maker and AIS is its glass partner from design to the assembly line; switching is slow and costly.
**Bad for price:** a customer that owns 10.6% and approves the related-party resolution has every reason to keep glass cheap. The auto margin has stayed in a 12-18% band through every cycle.

**A governance point:** shareholders, not only independent directors, must approve the Maruti transactions each year; the approval for FY27 (₹1,500 cr) is double FY26's actual sales, leaving room to grow.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** A narrow moat in automotive glass (scale, OEM approvals, a shareholder-customer), none in clear float glass. Returns on capital (ROCE 11-12% in FY25-26) have not covered a ~12% cost of capital through the last investment cycle.

sections.title: Revenue doubled in five years; profit is where it was in FY22 because float glass and new capacity swung the margin

blocks.p: AIS's revenue was ₹2,421 cr in FY21 and ₹4,982 cr in FY26: 15.5% a year. Automotive glass did most of the work (gross segment revenue ₹1,346 cr to ₹3,383 cr) as Indian car output recovered from Covid and each car carried more and better glass. Profit did not follow. Net profit jumped from ₹131 cr (FY21) to ₹343 cr (FY22) when import prices of float glass soared and AIS's float business earned a 34% EBITDA margin, then stalled at ₹325-367 cr for four years as float prices normalised, energy and soda ash rose (auto EBITDA margin 12% in FY23) and the new Soniyana float line and Patan auto capacity added depreciation (₹160 cr in FY23, ₹285 cr in FY26) and interest (₹105 cr to ₹204 cr) before they added profit. Because of the Sep-2025 QIP, FY26 EPS (₹13.8 reported, on weighted shares) was lower than in FY22 (₹14.2). The turn came in H2FY26: EBITDA of ₹250 cr, ₹287 cr and then ₹325 cr in Q1FY27 (23.0% margin), with profit ₹149 cr in Q1FY27 alone.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** AIS is two businesses with different economics. Automotive glass is a near-monopoly supplier to Indian car makers with steady 15-17% EBITDA margins and no pricing power over its customers. Float glass is a commodity whose profit is set by import prices, energy and trade policy; it made AIS look brilliant in FY22-23 and ordinary in FY24-25. The earnings recovery since H2FY26 is real, but most of it comes from float glass, the part of the business we trust least.

bullets: **Where the profit came from:** segment EBIT rose by ₹126 cr, of which float ₹80 cr and auto ₹45 cr. Interest fell ~20% after the QIP repaid debt.

**Costs:** raw materials fell to 22.75% of revenue (Screener; ~35% in Q1FY26) because AIS now makes the float glass it used to buy; power and fuel rose to ₹255 cr (18% of revenue) as the third float line ran full.
**Margins by our estimate:** auto EBITDA ~17.4%, float ~28.0% (quarterly segment depreciation is not disclosed).
**Maruti:** sales to Maruti ₹301 cr in the quarter (21% of revenue), vs ₹873 cr in the whole of FY26.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** with no calls and no guidance, investors extrapolate quarters. Q1FY27 annualises to ~₹1,300 cr of EBITDA and ~₹600 cr of profit; our FY27E (₹1,326 cr and ₹623 cr) is close to that run-rate. The question for the valuation is not FY27 but whether float margins of ~28% last into FY28-29.

sections.title: ₹2,835 cr of capex in three years, paid for with debt and a ₹1,000 cr QIP; returns have halved

blocks.p: Over FY21-23 AIS generated ₹1,504 cr of operating cash, spent ₹530 cr on capex and cut net debt from ₹1,693 cr (FY20) to ₹1,171 cr (FY23). Then it ran the largest investment programme in its history: ₹2,835 cr in FY24-26 (the third float line at Soniyana, Rajasthan; the Roorkee float cold repair; Patan phase 2; an on-site assembly unit inside Maruti's Kharkhoda plant), against ₹1,875 cr of operating cash. Net debt rose to ₹2,481 cr (FY25, 3.2x EBITDA) until a ₹1,000 cr QIP in Sep-2025 (1.18 crore shares at ₹845, +4.9% to the share count) repaid debt: ₹1,875 cr at Mar-2026 on Screener's basis (₹2,059 cr of borrowings on the company's). In Jan-2026 the board approved up to ₹2,000 cr more for greenfield float, coatings and processing capacity. Returns fell: ROCE 21% in FY22-23, 11% in FY26 (Screener), ROE 10.5%.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** the chairman writes that "the next phase must be about consolidation, optimisation, superior cash generation and higher returns" (AR FY26). Yet the next ₹2,000 cr is already approved, mostly for float glass, the business whose margin depends on import prices. If it is spent over FY27-29 as we assume, free cash flow stays near zero and net debt near ₹2,200 cr until the new capacity earns.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but grants in revenue, a weak cash year and a capitalisation-driven depreciation step-up

bullets: **Cash conversion was weak in FY26.** Cash from operations ₹502 cr, 55% of EBITDA (FY21-25: 51-119%), as inventories rose to ₹1,227 cr and receivables to ₹509 cr.

**Government grants sit in revenue.** ₹53.7 cr in FY26 (₹20.1 cr in FY25): ₹34.7 cr of GST-linked state investment incentives plus ₹18.9 cr released from a ₹329 cr capital grant booked in FY26 (balance ₹310 cr). That is ~6% of FY26 EBITDA; the capital-grant release continues at ~₹18 cr a year.

**Other income includes one-offs.** FY26 ₹48.9 cr: interest ₹15.7 cr, asset-sale gains ₹15.6 cr (incl. sales of assets to Maruti), write-backs ₹7.8 cr, miscellaneous ₹9.7 cr. We forecast ₹25-26 cr without asset-sale gains.
**Exceptional items:** FY26 ₹11.74 cr (labour-code past-service cost ₹7.20 cr and subsidiary merger costs ₹4.54 cr); FY25 +₹31.83 cr (gain). We forecast none.
**Related-party sales are large.** Maruti (a promoter) is 17.5% of revenue; prices are set in arm's-length negotiations per the company and approved by shareholders, but outsiders cannot test them.
**Depreciation and interest stepped up as projects were capitalised:** D&A ₹192 cr → ₹285 cr and interest ₹128 cr → ₹204 cr in FY26; Q1FY27 D&A ₹81 cr.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unmodified audit (VSSA & Associates) and simple accounts. The amber is for grants inside revenue, large related-party sales to a promoter-customer, asset-sale gains in other income and weak FY26 cash conversion.

sections.title: Net debt ₹1,875 cr (2.1x EBITDA) after the QIP; inventory is the big working-capital item

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 AIS had ₹2,198 cr of borrowings incl. leases (₹2,059 cr of debt on the company's basis: debt-equity 0.52x, debt/EBITDA 2.15x, down from 0.96x and 3.17x) against ₹323 cr of cash and investments: net debt ₹1,875 cr, 2.1x FY26 EBITDA. Net worth rose to ₹3,932 cr with the QIP. Glass making needs stocks of sand, soda ash and finished glass across 15 plants and 11 warehouses: inventories were ₹1,227 cr (~90 days of revenue), receivables only ₹509 cr (~37 days; car makers pay fast) and payables ₹891 cr. A ₹329 cr state capital grant for Soniyana was booked in FY26 as deferred income (in other liabilities) and is released into revenue at ~₹18 cr a year.

blocks.p: Promoters hold 51.58% (Jun-2026): AGC Inc. 21.18%, CMD Sanjay Labroo 11.47%, Maruti Suzuki 10.59% and other Labroo family and promoter-group holders ~8.3% (Mar-2026 names). Promoters fell from 54.09% to 51.58% when the Sep-2025 QIP added 4.9% to the share count; DIIs rose from 1.78% to 5.16% and FIIs from 3.74% to 4.87% in that quarter. Foreign portfolio investors held 4.85% and Indian institutions 5.26% at Jun-2026; ~64,157 shareholders. No promoter pledge reported in the sources we read.

Control is not contestable; free float is ~48% but institutions own only ~10%, so the stock trades on retail flows and is volatile.

sections.title: Governance: a family-run JV with a customer on the register; competent, not shareholder-first

blocks.p: Management: Sanjay Labroo (Chairman & Managing Director (promoter, 11.47%); term from 19-Feb-2024 for five years); Masao Fukami (Whole-time Executive Director since Jan-2023 (33 years in automotive glass, earlier at AGC's automotive-glass OEM office); re-appointment for four years from Jan-2027 recommended); Nisheeta Labroo (Non-executive director (promoter, relative of the CMD)); Shashank Srivastava (Non-executive director nominated by Maruti Suzuki, from Apr-2025); Kazuo Ninomiya (Non-executive director from Aug-2025 (replaced Masahiro Takeda on his retirement from AGC)). Pay: CMD ₹8.69 cr in FY26 = 2.5% of consolidated profit attributable to owners; independent directors ₹15-40 lakh commission each.

sections.title: The street: one broker, Buy, ₹1,050 on 22x FY28E EV/EBITDA

blocks.p: AIS is thinly covered. The only dated broker target we could verify as standing on 30-Sep-2026 is ICICI Securities' Buy with ₹1,050 (raised from ₹1,000), published after the Q4FY26 results (1-Jun-26): **22x FY28E EV/EBITDA**, on a ~10% EBIT CAGR over FY26-28E driven by value-added auto glass and the float ramp-up. Trendlyne's consensus page also showed a single analyst at ₹1,050. No broker note after the Q1FY27 results (5-Aug-2026) was visible to us. The stock closed at ₹959 on 30-Sep-2026, +10% below ICICI's target. ICICI Securities was a seller of the stock in 2023-24 (Sell at ₹484-503).

exhibit.title: Critiques we take seriously
head: Argument
Who
rows: Returns are low for the capital used: ROCE fell from 21% (FY22-23) to 11-12% (FY25-26) after ₹2,835 cr of capex in FY24-26; the chairman himself says 'the next phase must be about ... higher returns', yet another ₹2,000 cr is approved.
Float profits depend on trade protection: the Aug-2026 minimum import price lasts one year; FY22-23 showed what high import prices do (34% margin) and FY24-25 what imports do when they fall (18-20%).
Maruti is customer and promoter: ₹873 cr of sales in FY26 and approval for up to ₹1,500 cr in FY27 (30% of turnover) are related-party transactions; Maruti's bargaining power caps auto margins.
Equity dilution: the ₹1,000 cr QIP (Sep-2025) added 4.9% to the share count; FY26 EPS fell 9% (₹13.82 vs ₹15.27) even as profit before dilution was flat.
Q1FY27 looks like a peak: auto margins benefited from in-house float glass and record car volumes; the GST-boosted base arrives in Q3FY27.
Bull case (ICICI Securities): float capacity ramp-up and value-added auto glass drive double-digit EBIT growth; 22x FY28E EV/EBITDA.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a strong franchise at a full price, with float profits on borrowed time; SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the dominant supplier of car glass in India (~80% share), owned with its Japanese technology partner and its biggest customer, plus three float-glass lines that now make the company self-sufficient in raw glass. Earnings have just turned up sharply after a long, expensive build-out. Against that: auto margins capped by powerful customers, float profits that swing with import prices and depend today on trade protection, returns on capital below its cost, and another ₹2,000 cr of capex already approved.

**What you are paying:** 17.8x our Sep-28E EBITDA and 37.3x FY28E EPS, at a time when our numbers already assume float margins near their Q1FY27 level for FY27. Since 2021 the market has paid a median 18.1x forward EBITDA for AIS, and auto-component stocks were 13.4% below their five-year EV/EBITDA medians on 30-Sep-2026. On the street's own method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): SELL.

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Flat glass made by floating molten glass on a bath of molten tin; the raw material for windows, mirrors and car glass. A float line runs non-stop for 15+ years between "cold repairs".
Laminated: two sheets bonded with a plastic layer (windshields; holds together when broken). Tempered: heat-treated to be stronger and to break into small pieces (side and back glass).
Tonnes per day: the melting capacity of a float line.
Original equipment manufacturer: the vehicle maker (Maruti, Hyundai, Tata, Mahindra and others).
Gross includes sales to AIS's other segments (float glass sold to the auto business); external is sales to customers outside AIS.
The internal sales removed on consolidation so group revenue counts each sale once.
Minimum import price: imports below a set price are restricted. India set ₹34,000 a tonne on clear float glass for one year from 18-Aug-2026.
An extra import duty on goods sold in India below their home-market price; reviewed every five years ("sunset review").
Qualified institutional placement: a sale of new shares to institutions; AIS raised ₹1,000 cr in Sep-2025.
A deal with a shareholder, director or their companies; here mainly sales to Maruti Suzuki, a promoter.
Enterprise value (market value plus net debt) ÷ EBITDA; share price ÷ earnings per share.
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward figures the market will look at in September 2027.
How far comparable stocks trade below their own five-year median multiple on the valuation date.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the blended cost of debt and equity used to discount future cash.
Return on capital employed: operating profit ÷ debt plus equity.
